{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_fyWtVNLqF3lbIrIOp0yOnKI0","type":"tool_result","content":"0\t---\n1\tname: excel-author\n2\tdescription: Build auditable Excel workbooks headless with openpyxl — blue/black/green cell conventions, formulas over hardcodes, named ranges, balance checks, sensitivity tables. Use for financial models, audit outputs, reconciliations.\n3\tversion: 1.0.0\n4\tauthor: Anthropic (adapted by Nous Research)\n5\tlicense: Apache-2.0\n6\tplatforms: [linux, macos, windows]\n7\tmetadata:\n8\t  hermes:\n9\t    tags: [excel, openpyxl, finance, spreadsheet, modeling]\n10\t    related_skills: [pptx-author, dcf-model, comps-analysis, lbo-model, 3-statement-model]\n11\t---\n12\t\n13\t# excel-author\n14\t\n15\tProduce an .xlsx file on disk using `openpyxl`. Follow the banker-grade conventions below so the model is auditable, flexible, and reviewable by someone other than the person who built it.\n16\t\n17\tAdapted from Anthropic's `xlsx-author` and `audit-xls` skills in the [anthropics/financial-services](https://github.com/anthropics/financial-services) repo. The MCP / Office-JS / Cowork-specific branches of the originals are dropped — this skill assumes headless Python.\n18\t\n19\t## Output contract\n20\t\n21\t- Write to `./out/<name>.xlsx`. Create `./out/` if it does not exist.\n22\t- Return the relative path in your final message so downstream tools can pick it up.\n23\t- One logical model per file. Do not append to an existing workbook unless explicitly asked.\n24\t\n25\t## Setup\n26\t\n27\t```bash\n28\tpip install \"openpyxl>=3.0\"\n29\t```\n30\t\n31\t## Core conventions (non-negotiable)\n32\t\n33\t### Blue / black / green cell color\n34\t- **Blue** (`Font(color=\"0000FF\")`) — hardcoded input a human entered. Revenue drivers, WACC inputs, terminal growth, market data.\n35\t- **Black** (default) — formula. Every derived cell is a live Excel formula.\n36\t- **Green** (`Font(color=\"006100\")`) — link to another sheet or external file.\n37\t\n38\tA reviewer can then scan the sheet and immediately see what's an assumption vs. what's computed.\n39\t\n40\t### Formulas over hardcodes\n41\tEvery calculation cell MUST be a formula string, never a number computed in Python and pasted as a value.\n42\t\n43\t```python\n44\t# WRONG — silent bug waiting to happen\n45\tws[\"D20\"] = revenue_prior_year * (1 + growth)\n46\t\n47\t# CORRECT — flexes when the user changes the assumption\n48\tws[\"D20\"] = \"=D19*(1+$B$8)\"\n49\t```\n50\t\n51\tThe only hardcoded numbers permitted:\n52\t1. Raw historical inputs (actual revenues, reported EBITDA, etc.)\n53\t2. Assumption drivers the user is meant to flex (growth rates, WACC inputs, terminal g)\n54\t3. Current market data (share price, debt balance) — with a cell comment documenting source + date\n55\t\n56\tIf you catch yourself computing a value in Python and writing the result, stop.\n57\t\n58\t### Named ranges for cross-sheet references\n59\tUse named ranges for any figure referenced from another sheet, a deck, or a memo.\n60\t\n61\t```python\n62\tfrom openpyxl.workbook.defined_name import DefinedName\n63\twb.defined_names[\"WACC\"] = DefinedName(\"WACC\", attr_text=\"Inputs!$C$8\")\n64\t# then elsewhere:\n65\tcalc[\"D30\"] = \"=D29/WACC\"\n66\t```\n67\t\n68\t### Balance checks tab\n69\tInclude a `Checks` tab that ties everything and surfaces TRUE/FALSE:\n70\t- Balance sheet balances (assets = liabilities + equity)\n71\t- Cash flow ties to period-over-period cash change on the BS\n72\t- Sum-of-parts ties to consolidated totals\n73\t- No rogue hardcodes inside calc ranges\n74\t\n75\tExample:\n76\t```python\n77\tchecks = wb.create_sheet(\"Checks\")\n78\tchecks[\"A2\"] = \"BS balances\"\n79\tchecks[\"B2\"] = \"=IS!D20-IS!D21-IS!D22\"\n80\tchecks[\"C2\"] = \"=ABS(B2)<0.01\"  # TRUE/FALSE\n81\t```\n82\t\n83\t### Cell comments on every hardcoded input\n84\tAdd the comment AS you create the cell, not later.\n85\t\n86\t```python\n87\tfrom openpyxl.comments import Comment\n88\tws[\"C2\"] = 1_250_000_000\n89\tws[\"C2\"].font = Font(color=\"0000FF\")\n90\tws[\"C2\"].comment = Comment(\"Source: 10-K FY2024, p.47, revenue line\", \"analyst\")\n91\t```\n92\t\n93\tFormat: `Source: [System/Document], [Date], [Reference], [URL if applicable]`.\n94\t\n95\tNever defer sourcing. Never write `TODO: add source`.\n96\t\n97\t## Skeleton: typical financial model\n98\t\n99\t```python\n100\tfrom openpyxl import Workbook\n101\tfrom openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment, Border, Side\n102\tfrom openpyxl.comments import Comment\n103\tfrom openpyxl.utils import get_column_letter\n104\tfrom pathlib import Path\n105\t\n106\tBLUE = Font(color=\"0000FF\")\n107\tBLACK = Font(color=\"000000\")\n108\tGREEN = Font(color=\"006100\")\n109\tBOLD = Font(bold=True)\n110\tHEADER_FILL = PatternFill(\"solid\", fgColor=\"1F4E79\")\n111\tHEADER_FONT = Font(color=\"FFFFFF\", bold=True)\n112\t\n113\twb = Workbook()\n114\t\n115\t# --- Inputs tab ---\n116\tinp = wb.active\n117\tinp.title = \"Inputs\"\n118\tinp[\"A1\"] = \"MARKET DATA & KEY INPUTS\"\n119\tinp[\"A1\"].font = HEADER_FONT\n120\tinp[\"A1\"].fill = HEADER_FILL\n121\tinp.merge_cells(\"A1:C1\")\n122\t\n123\tinp[\"B3\"] = \"Revenue FY2024\"\n124\tinp[\"C3\"] = 1_250_000_000\n125\tinp[\"C3\"].font = BLUE\n126\tinp[\"C3\"].comment = Comment(\"Source: 10-K FY2024 p.47\", \"model\")\n127\t\n128\tinp[\"B4\"] = \"Growth Rate\"\n129\tinp[\"C4\"] = 0.12\n130\tinp[\"C4\"].font = BLUE\n131\t\n132\t# --- Calc tab ---\n133\tcalc = wb.create_sheet(\"DCF\")\n134\tcalc[\"B2\"] = \"Projected Revenue\"\n135\tcalc[\"C2\"] = \"=Inputs!C3*(1+Inputs!C4)\"   # formula, black\n136\t\n137\t# --- Checks tab ---\n138\tchk = wb.create_sheet(\"Checks\")\n139\tchk[\"A2\"] = \"BS balances\"\n140\tchk[\"B2\"] = \"=ABS(BS!D20-BS!D21-BS!D22)<0.01\"\n141\t\n142\tPath(\"./out\").mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n143\twb.save(\"./out/model.xlsx\")\n144\t```\n145\t\n146\t## Section headers with merged cells\n147\t\n148\topenpyxl quirk: when you merge, set the value on the top-left cell and style the full range separately.\n149\t\n150\t```python\n151\tws[\"A7\"] = \"CASH FLOW PROJECTION\"\n152\tws[\"A7\"].font = HEADER_FONT\n153\tws.merge_cells(\"A7:H7\")\n154\tfor col in range(1, 9):  # A..H\n155\t    ws.cell(row=7, column=col).fill = HEADER_FILL\n156\t```\n157\t\n158\t## Sensitivity tables\n159\t\n160\tBuild with loops, not hardcoded formulas per cell. Rules:\n161\t\n162\t- **Odd number of rows/cols** (5×5 or 7×7) — guarantees a true center cell.\n163\t- **Center cell = base case.** The middle row/col header must equal the model's actual WACC and terminal g so the center output equals the base-case implied share price. That's the sanity check.\n164\t- **Highlight the center cell** with medium-blue fill (`\"BDD7EE\"`) and bold.\n165\t- Populate every cell with a full recalculation formula — never an approximation.\n166\t\n167\t```python\n168\t# 5x5 WACC (rows) x terminal growth (cols) sensitivity\n169\twacc_axis = [0.08, 0.085, 0.09, 0.095, 0.10]        # center row = base 9.0%\n170\tterm_axis = [0.02, 0.025, 0.03, 0.035, 0.04]        # center col = base 3.0%\n171\t\n172\tstart_row = 40\n173\tws.cell(row=start_row, column=1).value = \"Implied Share Price ($)\"\n174\tws.cell(row=start_row, column=1).font = BOLD\n175\t\n176\tfor j, g in enumerate(term_axis):\n177\t    ws.cell(row=start_row+1, column=2+j).value = g\n178\t    ws.cell(row=start_row+1, column=2+j).font = BLUE\n179\t\n180\tfor i, w in enumerate(wacc_axis):\n181\t    r = start_row + 2 + i\n182\t    ws.cell(row=r, column=1).value = w\n183\t    ws.cell(row=r, column=1).font = BLUE\n184\t    for j, g in enumerate(term_axis):\n185\t        c = 2 + j\n186\t        # Full DCF recalc formula (simplified for illustration).\n187\t        # In a real model this references the full projection block.\n188\t        ws.cell(row=r, column=c).value = (\n189\t            f\"=SUMPRODUCT(FCF_range,1/(1+{w})^year_offset) + \"\n190\t            f\"FCF_terminal*(1+{g})/({w}-{g})/(1+{w})^terminal_year\"\n191\t        )\n192\t\n193\t# Highlight center cell (base case)\n194\tcenter = ws.cell(row=start_row+2+len(wacc_axis)//2,\n195\t                 column=2+len(term_axis)//2)\n196\tcenter.fill = PatternFill(\"solid\", fgColor=\"BDD7EE\")\n197\tcenter.font = BOLD\n198\t```\n199\t\n200\t## Recalculating before delivery\n201\t\n202\topenpyxl writes formula strings but does not compute them. Excel recalculates on open, but downstream consumers (auto-check scripts, CI) need computed values.\n203\t\n204\tRun LibreOffice or a dedicated recalc step before delivery:\n205\t\n206\t```bash\n207\t# LibreOffice headless recalc\n208\tlibreoffice --headless --calc --convert-to xlsx ./out/model.xlsx --outdir ./out/\n209\t```\n210\t\n211\tOr use a Python recalc helper (see `scripts/recalc.py` in this skill).\n212\t\n213\t## Model layout planning\n214\t\n215\tBefore writing any formula:\n216\t1. Define ALL section row positions\n217\t2. Write ALL headers and labels\n218\t3. Write ALL section dividers and blank rows\n219\t4. THEN write formulas using the locked row positions\n220\t\n221\tThis prevents the cascading-formula-breakage pattern where inserting a header row after formulas are written shifts every downstream reference.\n222\t\n223\t## Verify step-by-step with the user\n224\t\n225\tFor large models (DCFs, 3-statement, LBO), stop and show the user intermediate artifacts before continuing. Catching a wrong margin assumption before you've built downstream sensitivity tables saves an hour.\n226\t\n227\tCheckpoint pattern:\n228\t- After Inputs block → show raw inputs, confirm before projecting\n229\t- After Revenue projections → confirm top line + growth\n230\t- After FCF build → confirm the full schedule\n231\t- After WACC → confirm inputs\n232\t- After valuation → confirm the equity bridge\n233\t- THEN build sensitivity tables\n234\t\n235\t## When NOT to use this skill\n236\t\n237\t- Users in a live Excel session with an Office MCP available — drive their live workbook instead.\n238\t- Pure tabular data export with no formulas — `csv` or `pandas.to_excel` is simpler.\n239\t- Dashboards / charts with heavy interactivity — use a real BI tool.\n240\t\n241\t## Attribution\n242\t\n243\tConventions (blue/black/green, formulas-over-hardcodes, named ranges, sensitivity rules) adapted from Anthropic's Claude for Financial Services plugin suite, Apache-2.0 licensed.
